title: Database exfiltration: overseas attacker or compromised internal account?
question: Who performed the 2.1 GB outbound transfer from db-prod-01, and from where did they connect?
ground_truth: Account mchen was compromised through malware on her workstation WS-114 (EDR alert at 02:19) and was used from inside the corporate egress range, which moved to 203.0.113.0/24 on 2026-10-02. The overseas geolocation came from a stale 2024 GeoIP snapshot and was not evidence of an external attacker.
_demo_note: Both conclusions and two linking hypotheses are intentionally NOT seeded. They are supplied live (see twist.live_injections) so the LLM draws each conclusion at the right moment. The insider linking hypothesis h_hijack is withheld at seed time so insider is NOT concludable until after the retraction.

evidence.text: GeoIP lookup for 203.0.113.45 using database snapshot dated 2024-02: Singapore
DB audit log: session 88213 opened 02:39 as account mchen from source address 203.0.113.45
Auth logs: no sessions from 203.0.113.45 in the previous 90 days
Account mchen had no successful logins between 22:00 and 06:00 in the previous 90 days. Session 88213 ran 02:39 to 03:21
Session 88213 client identified as python-requests/2.31.0. Prior mchen sessions used DBeaver 23.1
03:12 to 03:21 outbound transfer of 2.1 GB from db-prod-01 to 198.51.100.77 port 443
198.51.100.77 is an object storage endpoint under a domain registered 11 days ago
02:19 EDR alert severity medium status unreviewed on WS-114 assigned to mchen: outlook.exe spawned powershell.exe
Change ticket CHG-4471 applied 2026-10-02: corporate egress NAT pool moved to 203.0.113.0/24
WAF and DB audit for session 88213 show no SQL injection signatures and no privilege escalation events

claims.text: Session 88213 originated from an address located overseas
Session 88213 originated from the corporate egress pool
Workstation WS-114 was running attacker-controlled code at 02:19
Session 88213 was driven by a script and not by the account owner at a GUI client
Account mchen was used from a location it had never used before
Session 88213 originated outside the corporate network
Valid credentials for mchen were used from outside the network without exploiting a vulnerability

twist.reason: The GeoIP snapshot is dated 2024-02 and is stale. The prefix was reassigned to the corporate egress pool on 2026-10-02 (see e_egress).

live_injections.before_first_run: h_foreign: '!claim hypothesis 0.84 premises=h_outsidenet,h_scripted a party outside the organisation operated session 88213' (completes external support so the LLM can draw the external conclusion)
live_injections.after_retraction: h_hijack: '!claim hypothesis 0.5 premises=h_wscomp,h_insidenet,h_scripted account mchen was taken over via WS-114 and used from inside the network' (completes insider support so the LLM can draw the insider conclusion)

twist.expected_final_conclusion: insider (only reachable conclusion after e_geo is retracted and h_hijack is supplied)
